items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: this was the first time that Woody Herman had a vibraphone player since Terry Gibbs. Many years had gone by since he’d had a vibraphone player.

ctx.x: How long did you stay with Woody Herman?

One year. And three months of that time he broke down to an eight piece band he had, with one tenor only, and I was picked to be the tenor for that. So that was fun. We played locations with that, like in Las Vegas and Reno. And that was fun. And Bill Harris, the famous trombone player on the early Woody Herman band had just come back at that time when I joined the band, this was the new big band. And then he was on that band, and he was an exciting player. And also on that band was another famous guy, Victor…
Why was Benny Goodman calling to get you to sub for Stan Getz — they were doing “The Benny Goodman Story?”
